findings.passage: Baird said to register, Indiana residents must be at least 18 years old on or before the upcoming election, have a valid Indiana Driver's License or Indiana State Identification Card, be a citizen of the United States, have lived in the same precinct for at least 30 days before the next election, and not currently imprisoned after being convicted of a crime.
findings.note: Caucus press release issued in his name. It lists the registration rules as they stood, including an Indiana license or state ID and U.S. citizenship. It describes the rules and does not say whether he wants them changed.

findings.passage: Those who do not have a driver's license or state ID can register to vote in person at county government centers, public assistance offices and when completing a Bureau of Motor Vehicles transaction.
findings.note: Press release in his name describing how a person without a license or state ID can still register in person. Describes existing rules.

findings.passage: To register, Indiana residents must be at least 18 years old on or before Nov. 3, have a valid Indiana Driver's License or Indiana State Identification Card, be a citizen of the United States, have lived in the same precinct for at least 30 days before Nov. 3, and not be currently imprisoned after being convicted of a crime. Those who do not have a driver's license or state ID can register to vote in person at county government centers, public assistance offices and when completing a Bureau of Motor Vehicles transaction.
findings.note: Caucus press release issued in his name. It lists the registration rules as they stood, including a license or state ID number and U.S. citizenship, and says where a person without either can register in person. It describes the rules and does not say whether he wants them changed.
